description:
OUTPOST COMMANDER is an independent, solo-built project team developing an educational lunar-outpost simulation for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Our project transforms lunar exploration science into an interactive mission experience where students manage power, oxygen, water, food, crew safety, and scientific research.

Core interests include software engineering, AI/ML, simulation design, data visualization, web development, and space exploration education.

OUTPOST COMMANDER is an educational lunar-outpost simulation developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge's "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge.

Players take command of a simulated research base near the Moon's south pole, balancing power, oxygen, water, food, and crew safety while managing infrastructure and lunar exploration.

The 13-Second Judge Quick Test introduces a power emergency, allowing players to make a critical decision and immediately observe its consequences through the simulation engine. Players can continue into the same mission state. Junior Astronaut Cadet Mode introduces interactive science checkpoints and learning badges covering lunar illumination, life-support systems, regolith shielding, and polar water-ice research.

The application also features a Gemini-powered Mission Advisor, NASA space-weather information, and NASA imagery. All game telemetry is simplified for educational purposes and is not operational spacecraft telemetry.
details:
About OUTPOST COMMANDER

OUTPOST COMMANDER is a browser-based educational lunar mission simulator created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

Set in a simulated research outpost near the lunar south pole, the application allows students to experience the challenges of operating a lunar base through interactive decisions and mission scenarios.

How It Works

Players manage five essential mission resources: Power, Oxygen, Water, Food, and Crew Safety.

The application includes five mission scenarios:

  • Standard Survival
  • Power Crisis
  • Water Shortage
  • Solar Storm Alert
  • Science Expansion

Players can construct and upgrade 12 infrastructure modules, assign astronauts to operational tasks, explore five lunar locations, research technologies, and respond to dynamic mission events.

Key Innovations

1. Judge Quick Test: A 13-second interactive demonstration where players experience a power emergency, make a real operational decision, and see its consequences. The resulting game state continues into Mission Day 2.

2. Junior Astronaut Cadet Mode: Guided science checkpoints on Days 1, 3, 5, and 7 introduce lunar illumination, life-support systems, regolith shielding, and polar water-ice research. Students earn learning badges and an in-game completion certificate.

3. Scientific Exploration: NASA DONKI solar-flare information and NASA imagery provide scientific context. The application also links to NASA research resources, including LRO Diviner, LOLA, LCROSS, and the Space Radiation Analysis Group.

4. Flight Director AI Advisor: A Gemini-powered assistant provides contextual recommendations based on the current simulation state, with a deterministic fallback when AI services are unavailable.

Technology Stack

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Node.js, Express, and Google's GenAI SDK (@google/genai).

Creativity and Impact

The project's main innovation is combining interactive lunar resource management with guided science education. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, students learn by making decisions, observing trade-offs, and understanding their consequences.

OUTPOST COMMANDER aims to make lunar exploration concepts more accessible and engaging for young learners.

Scientific Disclaimer: All resource values and mission outcomes are simplified educational simulation values. They do not represent operational NASA spacecraft telemetry, certified engineering specifications, or real astronaut safety predictions. NASA archive references are provided as scientific learning resources; only the explicitly identified live APIs are fetched by the application.
